3800: neuter of a presumed derivative of the same as ὀψάριον; rations for a soldier, i.e. (by extension) his stipend or pay:-- wages.
3801: ὁ ὢν καί ὁ ἦν καί ὁ ἐρχόμενος
ho ṑn kaí ho ēn kaí ho erchómenos
ho own kahee ho ane kahee ho er-khom'-en-os

a phrase combining ὁ with the present participle and imperfect of εἰμί and the present participle of ἔρχομαι by means of καί; the one being and the one that was and the one coming, i.e. the Eternal, as a divine epithet of Christ:--which art (is, was), and (which) wast (is, was), and art (is) to come (shalt be).
3803: from πήγνυμι; a trap (as fastened by a noose or notch); figuratively, a trick or statagem (temptation):--snare.
3804: from a presumed derivative of πάθος; something undergone, i.e. hardship or pain; subjectively, an emotion or influence:-- affection, affliction, motion, suffering.
3805: from the same as πάθημα; liable (i.e. doomed) to experience pain:--suffer.
3806: from the alternate of πάσχω; properly, suffering ("pathos"), i.e. (subjectively) a passion (especially concupiscence):-- (inordinate) affection, lust.
3807: from παῖς and a reduplicated form of ἄγω; a boy-leader, i.e. a servant whose office it was to take the children to school; (by implication, (figuratively) a tutor ("pædagogue")):-- instructor, schoolmaster.
3808: neuter of a presumed derivative of παῖς; a little boy:--child, lad.
3809: from παιδεύω; tutorage, i.e. education or training; by implication, disciplinary correction:--chastening, chastisement, instruction, nurture.
3810: from παιδεύω; a trainer, i.e. teacher or (by implication) discipliner:--which corrected, instructor.
3811: from παῖς; to train up a child, i.e. educate, or (by implication), discipline (by punishment):--chasten(-ise), instruct, learn, teach.
3812: adverb (of source) from παιδίον; from infancy:--of a child.
3813: neuter diminutive of παῖς; a childling (of either sex), i.e. (properly), an infant, or (by extension) a half-grown boy or girl; figuratively, an immature Christian:--(little, young) child, damsel.
3814: feminine diminutive of παῖς; a girl, i.e. (specially), a female slave or servant:--bondmaid(-woman), damsel, maid(-en).
3815: from παῖς; to sport (as a boy):--play.
3816: perhaps from παίω; a boy (as often beaten with impunity), or (by analogy), a girl, and (genitive case) a child; specially, a slave or servant (especially a minister to a king; and by eminence to God):--child, maid(-en), (man) servant, son, young man.
3817: a primary verb; to hit (as if by a single blow and less violently than τύπτω); specially, to sting (as a scorpion):--smite, strike.
3818: feminine of an adjective of uncertain derivation; Pacatianian, a section of Phrygia:--Pacatiana.
3819: probably another form for πάλιν (through the idea of retrocession); (adverbially) formerly, or (by relatively) sometime since; (elliptically as adjective) ancient:--any while, a great while ago, (of) old, in time past.
3820: from πάλαι; antique, i.e. not recent, worn out:--old.
3822: from παλαιός; to make (passively, become) worn out, or declare obsolete:--decay, make (wax) old.
3823: from (to vibrate; another form for βάλλω); wrestling:--+ wrestle.
3824: from πάλιν and γένεσις; (spiritual) rebirth (the state or the act), i.e. (figuratively) spiritual renovation; specially, Messianic restoration:--regeneration.
3825: probably from the same as πάλη (through the idea of oscillatory repetition); (adverbially) anew, i.e. (of place) back, (of time) once more, or (conjunctionally) furthermore or on the other hand:--again.
3826: dative case (adverb) of a compound of πᾶς and πλῆθος; in full multitude, i.e. concertedly or simultaneously:--all at once.
3827: from πᾶς and πολύς; full many, i.e. immense:--very great.
3828: from a compound of πᾶς and πυρά; every-tribal, i.e. heterogeneous (χώρα being implied); Pamphylia, a region of Asia Minor:--Pamphylia.
3829: neuter of a presumed compound of πᾶς and a derivative of δέχομαι; all-receptive, i.e. a public lodging-place (caravanserai or khan):--inn.
3830: from the same as πανδοχεῖον; an innkeeper (warden of a caravanserai):--host.
3831: from πᾶς and a derivative of ἀγορά; a mass-meeting, i.e. (figuratively) universal companionship:--general assembly.
3832: adverb from πᾶς and οἶκος; with the whole family:--with all his house.
3833: from a compound of πᾶς and ὅπλον; full armor ("panoply"):--all (whole) armour.
3834: from πανοῦργος; adroitness, i.e. (in a bad sense) trickery or sophistry:--(cunning) craftiness, subtilty.
3835: from πᾶς and ἔργον; all-working, i.e. adroit (shrewd):--crafty.
3836: adverb (of source) from πανταχοῦ; from all directions:--from every quarter.
3837: genitive case (as adverb of place) of a presumed derivative of πᾶς; universally:--in all places, everywhere.
3838: from πᾶς and τέλος; full-ended, i.e. entire (neuter as noun, completion):--+ in (no) wise, uttermost.
3840: adverb (of source) from πᾶς; from (i.e. on) all sides:--on every side, round about.
3841: from πᾶς and κράτος; the all-ruling, i.e. God (as absolute and universal sovereign):--Almighty, Omnipotent.
3842: from πᾶς and ὅτε; every when, i.e. at all times:--alway(-s), ever(-more).
3843: adverb from πᾶς; entirely; specially, at all events, (with negative, following) in no event:--by all means, altogether, at all, needs, no doubt, in (no) wise, surely.
3844: a primary preposition; properly, near; i.e. (with genitive case) from beside (literally or figuratively), (with dative case) at (or in) the vicinity of (objectively or subjectively), (with accusative case) to the proximity with (local (especially beyond or opposed to) or causal (on account of):--above, against, among, at, before, by, contrary to, X friend, from, + give (such things as they), + that (she) had, X his, in, more than, nigh unto, (out) of, past, save, side…by, in the sight of, than, (there-)fore, with. In compounds it retains the same variety of application.
3845: from παρά and the base of βάσις; to go contrary to, i.e. violate a command:--(by) transgress(-ion).
3846: from παρά and βάλλω; to throw alongside, i.e. (reflexively) to reach a place, or (figuratively) to liken:--arrive, compare.
3849: from παρά and the middle voice of βιάζω; to force contrary to (nature), i.e. compel (by entreaty):--constrain.
3850: from παραβάλλω; a similitude ("parable"), i.e. (symbolic) fictitious narrative (of common life conveying a moral), apothegm or adage:--comparison, figure, parable, proverb.
3851: from παρά and the middle voice of βουλεύω; to misconsult, i.e. disregard:--not (to) regard(-ing).
3853: from παρά and the base of ἄγγελος; to transmit a message, i.e. (by implication) to enjoin:--(give in) charge, (give) command(-ment), declare.
3854: from παρά and γίνομαι; to become near, i.e. approach (have arrived); by implication, to appear publicly:--come, go, be present.
3855: from παρά and ἄγω; to lead near, i.e. (reflexively or intransitively) to go along or away:--depart, pass (away, by, forth).
3856: from παρά and δειγματίζω; to show alongside (the public), i.e. expose to infamy:--make a public example, put to an open shame.
3857: of Oriental origin (compare פַּרְדֵּס); a park, i.e. (specially), an Eden (place of future happiness, "paradise"):--paradise.
3858: from παρά and δέχομαι; to accept near, i.e. admit or (by implication) delight in:--receive.
3859: from a compound of παρά and διατρίβω; misemployment, i.e. meddlesomeness:--perverse disputing.
3860: from παρά and δίδωμι; to surrender, i.e yield up, intrust, transmit:--betray, bring forth, cast, commit, deliver (up), give (over, up), hazard, put in prison, recommend.
3861: from παρά and δόξα (in the sense of seeming); contrary to expectation, i.e. extraordinary ("paradox"):--strange.
3862: from παραδίδωμι; transmission, i.e. (concretely) a precept; specially, the Jewish traditionary law:--ordinance, tradition.
3863: from παρά and ζηλόω; to stimulate alongside, i.e. excite to rivalry:--provoke to emulation (jealousy).
3864: from παρά and θάλασσα; along the sea, i.e. maritime (lacustrine):--upon the sea coast.
3865: from παρά and θεωρέω; to overlook or disregard:--neglect.
3866: from παρατίθημι; a deposit, i.e. (figuratively) trust:--committed unto.
3867: from παρά and αἰνέω; to mispraise, i.e. recommend or advise (a different course):--admonish, exhort.
3868: from παρά and the middle voice of αἰτέω; to beg off, i.e. deprecate, decline, shun:--avoid, (make) excuse, intreat, refuse, reject.
3869: from παρά and καθίζω; to sit down near:--sit.
3870: from παρά and καλέω; to call near, i.e. invite, invoke (by imploration, hortation or consolation):--beseech, call for, (be of good) comfort, desire, (give) exhort(-ation), intreat, pray.
3871: from παρά and καλύπτω; to cover alongside, i.e. veil (figuratively):--hide.
3872: from a compound of παρά and κατατίθημι; something put down alongside, i.e. a deposit (sacred trust):--that (thing) which is committed (un-)to (trust).
3873: from παρά and κεῖμαι; to lie near, i.e. be at hand (figuratively, be prompt or easy):--be present.
3874: from παρακαλέω; imploration, hortation, solace:--comfort, consolation, exhortation, intreaty.
3876: from παρακούω; inattention, i.e. (by implication) disobedience:--disobedience.
3877: from παρά and ἀκολουθέω; to follow near, i.e. (figuratively) attend (as a result), trace out, conform to:--attain, follow, fully know, have understanding.
3878: from παρά and ἀκούω; to mishear, i.e. (by implication) to disobey:--neglect to hear.
3879: from παρά and κύπτω; to bend beside, i.e. lean over (so as to peer within):--look (into), stoop down.
3880: from παρά and λαμβάνω; to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself (in any familiar or intimate act or relation); by analogy, to assume an office; figuratively, to learn:--receive, take (unto, with).
3881: from παρά and the middle voice of λέγω (in its original sense); (specially), to lay one's course near, i.e. sail past:--pass, sail by.
3882: from παρά and ἅλς; beside the salt (sea), i.e. maritime:--sea coast.
3883: from a compound of παρά and ἀλλάσσω; transmutation (of phase or orbit), i.e. (figuratively) fickleness:--variableness.
3884: from παρά and λογίζομαι; to misreckon, i.e. delude:--beguile, deceive.
3885: from a derivative of παραλύω; as if dissolved, i.e. "paralytic":--that had (sick of) the palsy.
3886: from παρά and λύω; to loosen beside, i.e. relax (perfect passive participle, paralyzed or enfeebled):--feeble, sick of the (taken with) palsy.
3887: from παρά and μένω; to stay near, i.e. remain (literally, tarry; or figuratively, be permanent, persevere):--abide, continue.
3888: from παρά and the middle voice of a derivative of μῦθος; to relate near, i.e. (by implication) encourage, console:--comfort.
3891: from a compound of παρά and νόμος; to be opposed to law, i.e. to transgress:--contrary to law.
3892: from the same as παρανομέω; transgression:--iniquity.
3893: from παρά and πικραίνω; to embitter alongside, i.e. (figuratively) to exasperate:--provoke.
3895: from παρά and πίπτω; to fall aside, i.e. (figuratively) to apostatize:--fall away.
3896: from παρά and πλέω; to sail near:--sail by.
3897: neuter of a compound of παρά and the base of πλησίον (as adverb); close by, i.e. (figuratively) almost:--nigh unto.
3898: adverb from the same as παραπλήσιον; in a manner near by, i.e. (figuratively) similarly:--likewise.
3899: from παρά and πορεύομαι; to travel near:--go, pass (by).
